messages:
ops-bot: INCIDENT SEV2 — GPU pool 'g-pool-prod' is at 98% allocatable GPUs; queue length spike detected. Autoscaler attempted 3 scale actions in 5m, all failed. Paging oncall. https://status.redwood-internal/incident/2950003333 :alarm:
carol: oncall hi - I'm on it. pinging infra and runtime. what metrics do we have?
alex: seeing massive queue growth on inference-router: token-inflight backlog up ~4.2x, head latency 95p > 1200ms, several customer requests timing out.
marta: autoscaler logs show repeated placement failures: "no compatible nodes for pod, fragment mismatch" and MIG allocation errors.
jing: attaching a recent scheduler dump:
```
E0305 12:07:02 scheduler.go:412] failed to allocate pod batch-req-432: no viable placement: MIG_SLOT_UNAVAILABLE
WARN  autoscaler.go:289] attempted scale up to 48 gpus, allocated 12 due to fragment constraints
INFO  pool-manager.go:122] stranded_slots=36, candidate_nodes=0
```
sam: that log line "stranded_slots=36" = GPUs present but not usable because MIG slices don't fit pod requests?
carol: correct. we recently rolled out a default MIG profile change (1g.4gb) for newer nodes — some older customer workloads request 2g slices and can't pack into mixed pools. autoscaler tries and exhausts headroom but can't place because binpacking fails.
alex: impact list from telemetry: 12 customers experiencing >=20% error rates, 6 seeing 504s from api-gateway. spike started ~12:02 UTC.
marta: attempted mitigation: increase autoscaler max to 96 from 64 — rejected by policy because cluster resource quota blocked further node creation. also, scale attempts are no-op due to placement failures per above.
jing: quick diagnostic commands run:
```
# show pool fragmentation
redwoodctl pool describe g-pool-prod --format=table
NODE    TOTAL_GPU  MIG_LAYOUT      FREE_MIG_SLOTS
n1      8          [1g,1g,1g,1g]    0
n2      4          [2g,2g]          0
n3      8          [1g,1g,1g,1g]    0
n4      4          [1g,1g]          2
# stranded count calc
redwoodctl pool stranded --pool g-pool-prod
STRANDED_GPUS: 36
```
carol: we need live mitigation. options: 1) emergency repack: drain and reassign pods to force better binpack, 2) temporarily allow CPU fallback for non-latency-critical customers, 3) change model-serving pod requests/limits to accept 1g slices where possible, 4) increase quota to create homogeneous nodes matching demand (2g slices).
sam: quick wins: patch the eviction controller to co-locate small slices on nodes with 2g leftovers? that's risky.
alex: we should triage customers: mark high-SLA tenants and failover them to dedicated pools (if they have reserved capacity).
marta: I'm starting an emergency repack run on a single subpool to validate — will do a canary on node n4->n2 sequence. command:
```
redwoodctl pool repack --pool g-pool-prod --nodes n4,n2 --dry-run
```
carol: good. while that's running, contact support to warn customers and open temporary status page note. @support-team can you draft a short message? Use exact wording: "We are investigating elevated error rates for some inference requests due to GPU placement constraints. Engineers are performing mitigation; no data compromise."
ops-bot: @support-team notified in #support.
sam: also adding an autoscaler override flag to ignore MIG profile mismatch for 10m to allow placement onto older nodes as emergency. downside: risk of degraded perf.
jing: patch CLI being tested:
```
# enable emergency ignore
redwoodctl autoscaler set-override --pool g-pool-prod --ignore-mig-profile=true --ttl=600
```
marta: repack dry-run shows improvement: predicted stranded drops to 8 in canary, expected latency improvement ~30% for canary tenants.
carol: proceed with canary repack on nodes n4,n2. coordinate with runtime to pause deployments during drain. alex, you'll handle customer failovers?
alex: yes, starting failover for top 3 SLA tenants to dedicated pools. will add temporary routing rules.
ops-bot: INCIDENT update: "Mitigation in progress — emergency repack and temporary autoscaler override applied to canary nodes. Some customers may see transient errors; we are failing over top SLAs."
marta: canary repack started: draining n4, cordon+evicting pods.
```
kubectl drain n4 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
redwoodctl pool repack --apply --nodes n4,n2
```
carol: monitor key metrics: queue length, 95p latency, error rate. set 5m cadence.
jing: initial canary metrics (5m after): queue length -22%, 95p latency -28%, errors for canary tenants down to baseline.
sam: autoscaler override in place for 10m; preparing to rollback if we see scheduling anomalies.
alex: failovers applied for tenant A,B,C. support notified customers A,B,C.
ops-bot: INCIDENT status: mitigation successful on canary. expanding repack to remaining nodes in 15m window.
carol: runbook items post-mitigation: 1) revert autoscaler override once repack completes, 2) schedule homogeneous node rollout (prefer 2g layout) for next maintenance window, 3) update default MIG profile docs, 4) evaluate adding fit-aware binpack algorithm to scheduler.
marta: opening a ticket: INFRA-9872 "GPU pool fragmentation: evaluate MIG default and autoscaler logic". assigning to infra and runtime.
jing: customer impact note for postmortem: "~12:02–12:40 UTC: elevated error rates for 12 customers; 6 experienced timeouts. Root cause: mixed MIG profiles across nodes causing heavy fragmentation and stranded GPUs, preventing autoscaler placements"
sam: I'll draft postmortem section on live mitigation and timeline.
carol: handoff to night oncall @alex in 30m — please monitor repack progress and rollback threshold: if median latency > 1s for >10m, revert and open escalation to platform leads.
alex: acknowledged. monitoring dashboard pinned. will update incident log and status page.
ops-bot: INCIDENT RESOLUTION PENDING — team continues to monitor.
carol: thanks everyone.
